Subject: Discovery Recap — Data Privacy & Logging Requirements

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture the immediate next steps. Please correct anything I missed.

Pain points you shared:
- Concern about PII surfacing in inference logs and embeddings (customer names, account numbers, SSNs in older transcripts).
- Need for configurable retention windows for different classes of data (end-user data vs. audit logs).
- Requirement for immutable, access-controlled audit logs for compliance reviews.
- Ability to redact sensitive content retrospectively and/or block it at ingestion.

Current stack you described:
- In-house LLM for internal workflows; some vendor endpoints for customer-facing features.
- Logs and artifacts stored in AWS S3; access via internal BI tools.
- SOC 2 in progress; security team owns controls and evidence collection.

Success criteria for any pilot with Redwood:
- No plain-PHI/PII stored in default application logs or embeddings unless explicitly allowed.
- Per-request controls to disable embeddings persistence and token-level redaction options.
- Configurable retention policies and an auditable, role-based access trail for any data kept.
- Ability to demonstrate evidence for SOC 2 (exportable audit logs, deletion proof).

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) We’ll send our security questionnaire (attached) for your security team to review — FinSecure can return with any gaps.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi to walk through redaction, retention controls, and KMS options (we suggested 10/08 PT below).
3) Share a short Data Flow / Retention matrix (Redwood) showing where data is cached, logged, or persisted by default and what controls exist to change that.

Attachments: FinSecure_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (attached)

If this aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite for the deep dive and loop in our compliance engineer.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Grace Chen <grace.chen@finsecure.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap — Data Privacy & Logging Requirements

Thanks Marissa — this is a good summary. A few clarifications / additional asks from security: 

1) Logs we need:
- Access logs (who queried what, when) — immutable for audit purposes.
- Session-level request/response data but with PII redacted by default. We need the option to retain session metadata for 90 days; audit logs must be retained up to 7 years for regulatory review.

2) Redaction requirements:
- We need deterministic redaction at ingestion (PII detection + remove/replace) and the ability to run retrospective redaction on historical logs.
- For embeddings: we must be able to opt-out of storing embeddings on a per-request basis; if stored, they must be encrypted and rotatable keys.

3) Evidence for SOC 2:
- Exportable audit trails showing access control changes, deletion events, and key rotation logs.

We’ll plan to include a couple folks from our security team on the technical deep dive: Paul R. (secops) and Siya M. (compliance).

One note: we prefer not to share production customer IDs in any logs/extracts — is there a way to pseudonymize before logs arrive to your system?

Appreciate you sending the Data Flow and retention matrix. We’ll review the questionnaire and get back with any follow-ups by EOD 10/07.

Best,
Grace Chen
Head of Product Security | FinSecure
grace.chen@finsecure.com

Looping internal next steps and tech questions for Rishi before the deep-dive. Rishi — can you prepare short answers for the items below and share any docs we can surface to FinSecure during the call?

Key technical asks from Grace/security:
- Deterministic PII detection & redaction: what approaches do we support (regex, ML models, custom detectors)? Support for post-hoc redaction?
- Embedding persistence controls: per-request flag to disable storing embeddings; if stored, encryption at-rest with customer-managed KMS and key rotation support.
- Deletion APIs: proof of deletion and deletion certificates for compliance evidence.
- Audit logs: immutable access logs, log retention controls, export formats (CSV/JSON) and signing options for tamper-evidence.
- Access controls: RBAC for log access + integration with their IdP (SAML/OIDC).
- Network controls: VPC/private endpoints and whether logs can be routed to their S3 directly.

Suggested deliverables for the call:
- Short (1-pg) Data Flow diagram showing where logs/embeddings are touched.
- Retention matrix mapping data types -> default retention -> configurable options.
- Short note on our KMS/HSM integrations and how we support RMK/CMK rotation.

Proposed timing: technical deep dive with Rishi + FinSecure secops on 2026-10-08 at 10:00 PT. Marissa — can you send the invite and include Paul and Siya?

Thanks,
Vanessa
